pairs.subject: quality-gates
pairs.evidence: lib/foundry/mesh/gates/rig-gate.ts:149 The rig gate reads skin weights, zero-weight vertices and the vertex count from the first primitive of the first mesh only. It still reports them as the whole asset ('N of M vertices carry no weight'), so a multi-primitive or multi-shell character passes with unweighted geometry the gate never saw, or fails as unrigged when its skin sits on a later mesh.

techniques.evidence: lib/foundry/mesh/gates/rig-gate.ts:149 The population is cut to one primitive by structure and reported in the same words as a whole-asset verdict. Morph targets are read across every mesh (line 129), so the narrower weight read is known, and nothing asserts it.
lib/foundry/mesh/gates/face-budget.ts:115 A missing request or measurement returns 'unmeasured' with a reason, never 'honored'. The rig gate also fails closed on unread joint names and morph counts.

lib/foundry/mesh/gates/mesh-score.ts:163 A component-count rule that misfired on assembled characters was narrowed with a face-share histogram, not deleted. The blunt rule stays wherever the histogram is absent.
lib/foundry/mesh/gates/mesh-score.ts:56 The thresholds are exported so the download door derives its ceiling from the number the grader uses, with no second hand-written copy.
lib/foundry/mesh/gates/mesh-score.ts:231 The three.js geometry scorer names the topology codes it cannot measure (GATE_ONLY_CODES) and does not let its green stand for them.
lib/foundry/mesh/gates/version.ts:6 Each GateResult carries the exact ported rule version that judged it, so a satisfied verdict points at the version it was measured on.
lib/foundry/mesh/gates/face-budget.ts:132 Budget findings name a remedy the reader can act on. The quad-trap branch points at providerFaceLimit, which ships in the same tree.
lib/foundry/mesh/gates/rig-gate.ts:376 Bytes the parser cannot read get their own outcome, separate from both pass and fail, and are never read as a clean rig.
